questions.q: What is the relationship between a virtual network (VNet) and a subnet in azurerm?
options: They are two names for the same resource type
A subnet is a smaller address range carved out of a VNet's larger address space
A VNet is carved out of a subnet
Subnets are only used for AKS clusters, never VMs
questions.explain: A VNet defines the overall address space (e.g. a /16), and subnets carve smaller ranges (e.g. a /24) out of it for specific resource groups.

questions.q: Why is azurerm_subnet_network_security_group_association needed as a separate resource?
options: Defining a network security group alone does not attach it to anything -- the association resource is what actually applies it to a subnet
It is purely optional documentation with no functional effect
It replaces the need for a network security group entirely
It is only required when using Windows virtual machines
questions.explain: An azurerm_network_security_group resource defines rules, but those rules only take effect once a separate association resource attaches the NSG to a subnet or NIC.

questions.q: In a security_rule block, how does Azure decide which rule to apply when multiple rules could match the same traffic?
options: Rules are applied in alphabetical order by name
The rule with the lowest priority number is evaluated first
The most recently created rule always wins
All matching rules are applied simultaneously
questions.explain: Security rules in an NSG are evaluated in order of their priority number, lowest first; the first matching rule determines the outcome.

questions.q: What does azurerm_network_interface connect to azurerm_linux_virtual_machine?
options: Nothing -- a VM does not require a network interface
The VM's operating system disk
The VM's network_interface_ids attribute, linking it to a subnet via the NIC's ip_configuration
The VM's admin_ssh_key block
questions.explain: network_interface_ids on the VM resource references the NIC, which in turn is placed in a subnet through its ip_configuration block.

questions.q: Why doesn't this lesson's Terraform configuration need to explicitly state the order resources are created in?
options: Terraform always creates resources in the order they appear in the file
Terraform creates all resources in parallel with no ordering
Terraform infers the dependency graph automatically from attribute references between resource blocks
Azure ignores creation order entirely
questions.explain: Because resources reference each other's attributes (e.g. a subnet referencing a VNet's name), Terraform builds a dependency graph and orders creation automatically.
